newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-- Differentials remain rangebound.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-- Differentials remain rangebound.

text.p: U.S. spot product differentials were little changed Monday afternoon from those seen late last week as the market remained locked into a stable trading range, players said.

But firmer NYMEX futures gave a moderate boost to absolute prices as the cash market awaited direction to break its differential stalemate. July gasoline jumped 0.65 cent to 58.05 cents a gallon by 1254 EDT (1654 GMT), while heating oil rose 0.46 cent to 52.10 cents.
Heating oil for delivery during the front-18th cycle over the Colonial Pipeline was offered at 2.25 cents below July futures, stable with Friday values.
"Gulf heat has been trading in the minus 2.25-cent to minus 2.10 cent range for weeks. The market sold off over a month ago and seems comfortable there," a Gulf Coast trader said.

Although diffs were in a stalemate, he noted they were holding their own in a season of weak demand in large part because of contango on the NYMEX, with outer-month barrels priced high enough to encourage stock building.
Gulf low sulfur diesel firmed a trace to 1.50 cents under the July print for front-18th-cycle material, players said, amid talk of European inquiries about two Gulf Coast cargoes.

Gulf "M1" conventional unleaded gasoline differentials were stable at 2.80 cents below the July print, traders said, despite the approach of Tuesday's scheduling deadline for front-18th-cyle "M-grade" barrels.

"The prompt cycle is not strengthing at all despite the deadline," one Gulf player said, adding that prompt diffs usually gain strength as the deadline draws near for scheduling barrels on the Colonial.
"One reason may be that people bought early this time around. They got caught short in previous cycles and had to pay a premium" to secure barrels, the trader said.

Prompt "M2" conventional unleaded gasoline was offered at 2.25 cents below July futures, a smidgen firmer than Friday diffs, with "A2" grade reformulated little changed at about 0.25 cent below the July screen, traders said.
Prompt "V2" 93-octane premium was sold for 5.0 cents over July NYMEX, traders said, a half cent firmer than Friday diffs. NYH heating oil offers edged a trace higher to 0.70
cent above the July print after Sun Co posted a new price of 0.60 cent over the print, players said.

Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials were about a quarter cent to half cent weaker amid little demand, players said. Group Three unleaded differentials were about 4.50/4.75 cents over NYMEX July gasoline. Chicago markets were pegged 3.50/3.75 cents over the print in quiet activity.
No deals were yet heard done.

Low sulphur differentials were pegged steady, also due to quiet activity. Group Three material was between 3.75/4.00 cents over the screen, although players said they forecast values to firm slightly amid a slight tick-up in demand for the wheat harvest.
